MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center

PATIENT: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
SEX: Male
SPECIMEN: Peripheral blood
COLLECTION DATE: [redacted date]
REPORT DATE: [redacted date]

REFERRING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]

TEST PERFORMED
Sex Chromosome Analysis by PCR

METHODOLOGY
Quantitative fluorescence PCR (QF-PCR) was performed to detect sex chromosome aneuploidies. DNA was extracted from peripheral blood and analyzed using multiplex PCR with fluorescently labeled primers targeting amelogenin and STR markers on chromosomes X and Y. Fragment analysis was performed by capillary electrophoresis.

RESULTS
Sex Chromosome Complement: XXY

The PCR analysis detected an XXY sex chromosome complement, consistent with Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY).

INTERPRETATION
The presence of XXY sex chromosomes confirms the diagnosis of Klinefelter syndrome. This is a chromosomal condition affecting males, characterized by the presence of an extra X chromosome. The molecular findings are diagnostic, making further cytogenetic analysis unnecessary.

FOLLOW-UP
G-banding karyotype analysis has been canceled based on the definitive PCR results. The fixed cell suspension from this specimen will be stored for 3 months per laboratory protocol should additional testing be required.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss the implications of this diagnosis
2. Endocrine evaluation for testosterone replacement therapy consideration
3. Fertility assessment and counseling regarding reproductive options
4. Monitoring for associated medical conditions

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory.

Electronically signed by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
